title: Whole genome, whole exome, and targeted sequencing of high-grade meningioma tumor samples
corresponding_author: Sandro Santagata / Ian F. Dunn / Rameen Beroukhim
institution: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute / Brigham and Women's Hospital, Harvard Medical School
needs_manual_review_reason: NEW RECORD (2026-07-11). Verified live via the EGA Metadata API: study EGAS00001002294 ('Whole genome, whole exome, and targeted sequencing of high-grade meningioma tumor samples') has exactly one registered dataset, EGAD00001003220 ('High-grade meningioma sequencing data'), num_samples=188 (confirmed via /datasets/EGAD00001003220/samples: 143 tumor + 45 normal/blood, 125 unique subject_id patients), dataset_types=['Exome sequencing','Whole genome sequencing']. THREE DIFFERENT SAMPLE-COUNT NARRATIVES were found across the live sources and could not be fully reconciled, flagging per instructions: (1) the EGAS study-level description text states 'we analyzed the genomes of 274 high-grade meningiomas and compared this information with data from 456 low-grade meningiomas' (274/456, a broader multi-cohort framing that does not match any single deposited dataset); (2) the actual live PMC full text of the linked paper (PMID 28713588, post-erratum PMC version, erratum PMID 29263836 corrected an original miscount) states 'we analyzed the genomes of 134 high-grade meningiomas and compared this information with data from 595 previously published meningiomas', built from a discovery cohort of 66 tumor samples/39 individuals (WGS+WES) extended with targeted sequencing of 76 additional samples (39+76 does not cleanly equal 134, likely due to overlap/recurrences counted differently); (3) the actually deposited EGAD00001003220 dataset itself, which is the only concrete public artifact and forms the basis of this record's sample_count/patient_count fields, contains 188 total BAM files (143 tumor, 45 normal) from 125 patients. Given the instruction to prioritize what the live dataset itself shows, sample_count=188 and patient_count=125 are used here, distinct from both narrative totals in the paper and the EGAS description; a human pass should decide if the discrepancy needs a clarifying note to end users. Modality: the dataset's own free-text description says 'Whole genome, whole exome, and custom panel sequencing of high-grade meningioma cohort,' but the formal categorical dataset_types field returned by the live API only lists Exome sequencing and Whole genome sequencing (no targeted-panel category), so modality here is conservatively set to ['wgs','wes'] only; the mismatch between the free-text 'custom panel sequencing' mention and the absence of a corresponding categorical/vocabulary tag is flagged for reviewer attention rather than guessed. grade_breakdown left null because the live sample metadata only exposes tumor/normal phenotype, not per-sample WHO grade 2 vs 3 split, despite the whole cohort being 'high-grade' by the study's own inclusion criterion. Corresponding author taken from PMC full-text XML corresp='yes' tags (Santagata, Dunn IF, Beroukhim all marked corresponding). publication_status set to 'corrected' because PMID 28713588 has a formal published Erratum (PMID 29263836, Sep 2017) altering the reported sample totals; the erratum-corrected numbers are what is reflected above. Only public EGA study/dataset-level metadata was used; the controlled-access sequencing data itself was never accessed, per docs/scope.md. AUDIT 2026-07-12 (external re-verification): sex_distribution added ('61 female, 64 male (125 patients)') from the live /datasets/EGAD00001003220/samples biological_sex field, which is exposed for all 188 registered samples (95 female / 93 male at the sample level) and is internally consistent per subject_id, resolving to 61 female and 64 male across the 125 unique patients; previously 'Not reported'. sample_count (188), patient_count (125), normal_control_tissue count (45), publication metadata (PMID 28713588, erratum PMID 29263836, DOI 10.1038/s41525-017-0014-7) and all other fields re-verified correct against the live EGA API and PubMed this pass.
